strengths: Novel problem formulation and first comprehensive global-scale audio geolocation benchmark with new datasets (iNatSounds benchmark setup and XCDC with 576 species-rich recordings)

Well-designed experimental evaluation with clear baselines, clever species oracle experiments using SINR range maps providing informative upper bounds (97.8% region accuracy), and comprehensive ablations across components

Important insights identifying species identification as the critical bottleneck—the 95 percentage point gap between oracle (97.8%) and best method (17.2%) region accuracy clearly contextualizes fundamental challenges

Thorough experimental work with standard deviations across 3 runs, appropriate evaluation metrics across geographic scales, and honest treatment of limitations including geographic bias and distribution shift to XCDC
Extensive supplementary material supporting reproducibility with detailed implementation details, hyperparameters, and computation resources
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: AG-CLIP is a straightforward addition of a species checklist decoder to GeoCLIP; other methods are basic adaptations of existing approaches (regression, classification, retrieval); vision-inspired spectrogram approach is standard practice not justified over alternatives

Modest and limited performance with concerning generalization: 17.2% region accuracy on iNatSounds drops dramatically to 4.3% on species-rich XCDC, indicating poor generalization to natural multi-species scenarios despite same ecological domain

Fundamental bottleneck limits practical impact: paper demonstrates species identification is the binding constraint (2.5% vs 25.8% region accuracy with predicted vs true species on XCDC), but this is outside the scope and reduces real-world applicability

Underdeveloped multimodal geo-forensics component: only 4 movie clips with purely qualitative evaluation, no systematic analysis, no dataset created; divergences noted but not explained; feels like an afterthought that dilutes paper focus

Significant geographic bias with performance variation: iNatSounds heavily biased toward North America/Europe with clear spatial disparities (good performance in US/Europe, poor in Africa/Asia); distribution shift to XCDC suggests fundamental generalization issues

Paper tries to cover too much ground (core geolocation, species-rich recordings, spatiotemporal aggregation, multimodal forensics), weakening execution and focus; spatiotemporal aggregation experiments are artificial (year-long aggregation unrealistic in practice)

Overstated novelty claims: called 'first study' but primarily a benchmarking contribution building on existing image geolocation methods; earlier audio geolocation studies exist (refs 14, 25, 26, 40, 48)

Missing analysis of what signals AG-CLIP learns, auxiliary checklist loss provides only marginal improvements (2.7% at continent level), and limited investigation into failure modes despite spatial variation shown in results
